title: Choose the visual world for ClipPass
question: The roll assigned Edge-Code Reel. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Edge-Code Reel
options.lineage: 35mm colour negative stock and its keycode edge print, read on an editor's lightbox
options.thesis: Every license is a frame on the reel, and its edge code is the Stellar transaction.
options.viewport: A WebGL strip of orange negative crosses a lit lightbox; frames fill lane by lane, the exclusive frame fogs at the 1 XLM gate, and the script form is the leader you write on.
options.risk: Film nostalgia reads as costume if the edge codes decorate instead of carrying real tx hashes.

raised.raise: Light is the state: only the frame in the projector gate is lit; everything else sits unlit on the lightbox.
Registration marks the active frame: it locks onto the pin, the rest of the strip rides a hair off register.
Decisions stay on the film as history: every skip and refusal leaves its grease-pencil mark on the leader.
Total palette commitment: base orange, frame black, edge-print yellow; red exists only for a refusal.
Film artifacts fire on exact events (a paid frame flares, the refusal fogs), never as a constant filter.

options.label: Grease-Pencil Contact Sheet
options.lineage: darkroom contact sheets marked up by picture editors
options.thesis: The agent edits like a picture editor: circles the keepers, crosses out what the card refused.
options.viewport: A full contact sheet of every candidate asset, frames circled in red as they are licensed, with the script form pinned at the sheet's margin.
options.risk: The most familiar route for media products; a flat paper sheet gives the 3D the least to do.

options.label: VU-Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Each lane is a meter; the card limit is the red past zero.
options.viewport: Four meters (SFX, B-roll, Music, Exclusive) across a desk bridge; needles swing to each price and the exclusive pins hard into the red.
options.case: Fuses cleanly for the card limit; loses on the reel and the license sheet, which have no home on a desk.
options.risk: Studio-gear skeuomorphism can feel like a music app rather than a licensing agent.

options.label: Hand-Processed 16mm
options.thesis: Emulsion damage joins the photographed event.
options.viewport: A boiling grain strip with light leaks flooding the perforations.
options.case: Same film family as the roll, with grain and scratches that cost the facts their legibility.
options.risk: Damage aesthetics fight a license sheet that must read on a projector.
options.kept: Artifacts fire on exact events, never as a constant filter.

options.label: Akari Workshop
options.thesis: Folded paper volumes lit from within.
options.viewport: Glowing paper volumes hanging in a dim room.
options.case: Creators and judges have no route from paper lamps to licensing reels.
options.risk: Serene and unrelated to the product's mechanism.
options.kept: Light is the state: only the active frame is lit.

options.label: Ben-Day Comic Page
options.thesis: Six panels, six licenses, four-colour misregistration.
options.viewport: A six-panel grid with the exclusive as a splash panel.
options.case: Panels map to assets, but comics pull the story away from film licensing and real proof.
options.risk: Reads as a joke at exactly the moment the payment proof must read as serious.

options.label: Flash-and-Scrawl Sleeve
options.thesis: A flash photo defaced with marker.
options.viewport: A blown-out party photo with a scrawled logo.
options.case: Music-culture energy, but the defaced surface buries prices and tx links.
options.risk: Illegible on a projector; no real photography exists to deface.
options.kept: Decisions leave marks that stay on the surface as history.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: Linked black-and-white cards you can paint.
options.viewport: A card stack with painted buttons linking each step.
options.case: Neither creators nor judges identify with it, and one-bit cannot show a refusal by colour.
options.risk: Pure retro novelty for this audience.
options.kept: Total palette commitment, with colour reserved for one state.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: An AI-agent payments dashboard, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A headline and form on the left, a live agent panel and stat cards on the right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every Web3 agent demo by design.
